evidence_summary: Effects Database identifies the pedal as produced in the United States by United Musical Industries and places it in the late-1960s to early-1970s period. A surviving 1968 example provides specimen-level chronology.

Gearphoria identifies UMI as the maker of a Tone Booster and notes that the same product exists under different brand names whose manufacturers were not identified. The UMI attribution is retained, while alternate labels remain unresolved.

Gearphoria's period-focused UMI feature identifies the Treble-Bass Booster & Mute as one of three UMI pedals shown from the collection, alongside Buzz Tone and Wa Pedal. Effects Database identifies the UMI catalog as a four-product set including this pedal.

A surviving UMI Wa example carries an original CTS pot dated week 18 of 1969. Multiple specialist sources identify the Wa Pedal as a UMI product founded by Richard Soloway's company in Farmingdale, New York.

Effects Database groups Apollo No. 843 with UMI-made Conrad and UMI Buzz Tone products in the same Buzz Box & Volume Expander family. The UMI relationship is treated as a marketed-label/OEM state, not as an independent Apollo factory.
Effects Database identifies the Conrad Buzz Box & Volume Expander as a UMI-related marketed state and directly lists it with Apollo No. 843 and UMI Buzz Tone in the related family.

Effects Database describes UMI as founded by Richard Soloway in Farmingdale, New York around 1967. Gearphoria independently dates the company's founding to 1967 and identifies amps as its first products before pedals.

Current source set supports four direct UMI pedal products: Buzz Tone & Volume Expander, Tone Booster, Treble-Bass Booster & Mute, and Wa Pedal. Other related products such as Kimberly, Audio Designs, and Applied products are kept separate unless model-specific evidence identifies UMI manufacture.
